variables.definition: The average temperature of the air 2 metres above the ground, the height standard weather stations measure at.
variables.caveat: Reanalysis 2-metre temperature can diverge from surface-station records over the Indo-Gangetic Plain, where station data show stronger warming. Regional results there deserve extra caution.

variables.definition: The highest air temperature reached each month, 2 metres above the ground. Reflects how hot days become.
The lowest air temperature reached each month, 2 metres above the ground. Reflects how cold nights become.
All rain and snow that reaches the ground, bias-corrected against ground stations. Monthly values are averages in millimetres per day; the tool converts them to totals.
variables.caution: Rainfall alone cannot establish drought or aridity; combine with soil wetness and evaporation.
variables.known_divergence: MERRA-2 precipitation over South Asia shows stronger wetting trends than observed datasets (GPCP). Always check the GPCP observed cross-check panel for this variable.

variables.definition: How close the air is to saturation with water vapour (100% = fully saturated).
The average speed of wind 10 metres above the ground.
How wet the topmost soil layer is, from 0 (bone dry) to 1 (saturated), estimated by a land surface model.
variables.caution: Model estimate, not a measurement; drought assessment needs more than one variable.

variables.definition: Water evaporated from land and plants into the air. Monthly values are averages in millimetres per day; the tool converts them to totals.
